- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >65.00) — cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.0% from next forecast to align with recent trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price movements by 1–2 days — adjust forecast to be 1–2% higher than true outcome for the first 2–3 days of the horizon.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
